content:
Chess is a classic board game for two players, commonly introduced to beginners as a game of strategy and skill. It is played on a square board with 64 squares arranged in an 8×8 grid. Each player, called "White" and "Black," begins with sixteen pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights, and eight pawns. The pieces are set up in a specific arrangement at the start of the game, with White's pieces on the first two ranks and Black's on the last two ranks. White always moves first, and players alternate turns.

Each type of piece moves differently. For example, rooks move any number of squares horizontally or vertically, bishops move diagonally, knights move in an L-shape, pawns move forward one square (with the option to move two squares on their first move), the queen combines the powers of rook and bishop, and the king moves one square in any direction. A player may capture an opponent's piece by moving their own piece onto the square occupied by that piece.

The main objective is to checkmate the opponent's king, which means putting the king under threat of capture ("in check") with no legal move to escape the threat. If this occurs, the game ends immediately. There are also several ways a game can end in a draw, such as stalemate (when a player has no legal moves and is not in check), insufficient material to checkmate, threefold repetition of the same position, or the fifty-move rule (when fifty moves have passed without a pawn move or capture).
